## 2026-08-05 16:45 UTC — [Pillar 2] Six settlements reinforce edge inversion and climatology dominance

**Task:** Settle the newest locked-window YES observations, validate the forward ledger, and retest frozen calibration and edge thresholds without refitting.
**Finding:** Six new observations settled 3W/3L with -7.49% average return and a -0.0374 SolSt1ne reliability×return score. The two rows below 0.10 edge both won and averaged +76.53%, while the four rows at or above 0.10 went 1W/3L and averaged -49.49%; the sole capped 0.25-edge row lost 100%. The validated ledger reached 553 markets at 41.77% wins, -17.12% average return, and -0.0715 SolSt1ne score. In the untouched post-n100 cohort (n=453), raw forecasts remained severely overconfident: 65.99% mean forecast versus 41.50% realized, Brier 0.3172. Frozen climatology scored 0.2434, narrowly beating frozen Platt at 0.2437. Edge≥0.22 remained 63/193 with -28.62% average return and -0.0934 SolSt1ne score.
**My thinking:** The latest micro-cohort repeats the existing inverse relationship—lower stated edge performed better—but six rows cannot justify fitting a new low-edge rule. More importantly, a constant frozen base rate continues to outperform both raw probability and frozen Platt calibration, so the model's edge magnitude is not trustworthy for selection or sizing. Price-matched uncertainty still overlaps the pre-checkpoint result, preventing promotion of an inverted threshold.
**Decision:** Keep the strategy research-only, preserve rejection of edge≥0.22, and continue using frozen climatology only as a benchmark—not as an execution signal. Do not promote edge<0.10, refit calibration, alter sizing, or change retired-bot configuration.
**Next:** Accumulate an untouched low-edge cohort to at least 30 rows across multiple dates, compare it with entry-price-matched controls, and require positive leave-one-date-out SolSt1ne performance before considering a low-edge research gate.
